messages:
alex: Heads up — saw a perf regression on the 8xA100 job (tp=3 pp=2, kv sharded across TP slices). Throughput dropped ~22% after the batching heuristic change last night.

maria: ugh, any obvious hotspot in the profile? :thinking_face:

alex: nsys capture attached to the job logs. Main symptom is a long all-reduce at step boundary ~6-8ms that wasn't there before. KV stash serialization looks fine.

ravi: can you paste the nsys summary lines? quick grep?

alex: sure — pasted below: 
```
CUDA kernels: compute 12.3ms, memcpy 0.8ms, allreduce 7.9ms
Comm timeline: all-reduce start 12.5ms end 20.4ms (per-iter)
KV update: net serialize 0.4ms
Batcher: flush window 16ms -> now 24ms
```

sophie: that flush window bump would increase per-step wait — looks like the dynamic_batcher change forced bigger micro-batches to align which pushes overlap out of sweet spot.

maria: hypothesis: before the change we overlapped compute + allreduce better because KV cache shards were smaller (TP-local) so less cross-device traffic. After change, KV slices got coalesced and now we hit pp boundary exchanges.

ravi: interesting — so TP sharding kept KV local to the tensor-slice GPUs, PP placement requires doing an all-reduce or point-to-point during stage transitions?

sophie: yup. With PP the KV must be visible to the later pipeline stage which is on different ranks. If we shard per-TP slice but then pipeline-schedule spreads attention, we either replicate or we do an all-reduce at boundary. We chose the latter for mem savings.

alex: replication (DP style) would eliminate that all-reduce but costs ~x GPUs memory; with our rp quant profile for 70B it's borderline.

maria: could we try hybrid: keep KV replicated across GPUs within a PP stage (i.e., replicate per-stage, shard across TP inside a stage)? minimizes cross-stage comm but doesn't blow up memory as full DP replication does.

ravi: that's what we call "stage-local replication" in notes. Implementation: at model load time, do an ncclBroadcast for KV shard to all ranks in the same pipeline stage. Then intra-stage access is local. Only inter-stage pipeline transfer is needed for activations, not KV all-reduce.

sophie: another knob — increase background async memcpy overlap. If we move KV exchange earlier (prefetch during token generation) we could hide some of the all-reduce in compute. But that relies on batching hitting predictable patterns.

alex: repro plan: 1) revert batching heuristic to prior config, 2) run stage-local replication experiment, 3) run async-prefetch variant. I'll run 1 and 2 overnight and post perf numbers.

perf-bot: [regression-alert] job id: rwd-infer-4021 flagged: throughput -22% vs baseline 2026-03-07 03:12 UTC

maria: thanks. if you can prod out nsys traces for both stage-local-rep and revert, we can compare the comm/compute overlap waterfall and quantify wallclock savings.

alex: will do. adding checklist: `--trace=nsys --batcher-config=prev` and `--kv-mode=stage-rep`

sophie: small note: measurement must use steady-state 2000 iters to avoid startup noise. Also pin CUDA streams for the async path test.

alex: noted. I'll upload results tomorrow. :thumbsup:

maria: awesome — if we confirm, this could be a default for TP+PP combos on the 40-70B families. Less memory than DP, better perf than pure-sharded all-reduce.

ravi: cc @infra-team for possible scheduler tweaks if we need co-located stage ranks.

maria: good call. thanks everyone.
